claims.quote: "We will make a civic pledge. We will offer the kitchens and a measured rotation of labour hours as a civic contribution. We will not hand names. We will keep records so that any claim may be accounted for and argued on the house's terms. I will instruct the clerks to draw a civic ledger entry now, stating what we pledge to spare."
claims.value: Headmistress pledged kitchens and measured labour hours as civic contribution; instructed clerks to record civic pledge in house logs

claims.quote: People divided as if by geography... clerks and registry women... instructors and older apprentices... Voices rose in the low, urgent way of people who had worked in close quarters for years.
claims.value: Academy divided into factions for bargaining vs fortifying

claims.quote: "Counting is what we do," he said, "but beware that counts become chains. We can offer hours and skill; we cannot make the girls into columns on an enemy's tally."
claims.value: Loren cautions that accounting can turn into chains; warns against binding people as counts

claims.quote: A clerk moved to a drawer and produced a narrow register... "Civic pledge—kitchens, rotation of labour to be scheduled and recorded," he murmured as he wrote the heading aloud.
claims.value: Clerk began to record civic pledge heading in a register; pledge to be logged in house records

claims.quote: "Rue thought of her own signing, the wax, the signet, the seam where 'tethering' had been written. She felt pulled: to the Headmistress, who preserved roofs and work; to Loren, who warned that counted hours could harden into obligations no one meant to sign for."
claims.value: Rue torn between defending Academy and acknowledging its costs; internal conflict recorded
